title: Zinc Fizzes, Copper Stays Silent: Electrode Potentials of the 3d Metals
subject: Chemistry
objective: Copper is the only 3d metal with a positive E°(M²⁺/M) (+0.34 V), so it gives no H₂ with dilute acids. Turning Cu(s) into Cu²⁺(aq) costs more (atomisation + two ionisations) than hydration pays back: 921 against zinc's 711 kJ/mol. Stable d⁵ and d¹⁰ bend the trend: Mn and Zn dip, Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidant, Fe³⁺ is stable.

tf.q: Zinc liberates H₂ from dilute HCl.
Copper dissolves in nitric acid with evolution of H₂.
tf.explain: It dissolves, but the acid is reduced; no H₂.

ar.a: Copper does not liberate H₂ from dilute acids.
E° of Zn is more negative than the trend.
ar.r: Zn²⁺ has a stable d¹⁰ configuration.

short.q: Why is Cr²⁺ reducing while Mn³⁺ is oxidising, though both are d⁴?
short.solution: Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives d³ (half-filled t₂g, more stable), so it loses an electron easily; Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives the half-filled d⁵, so it gains one easily.
